title: An Examen Without a Clock
reflection:
The Examen has never needed a fixed hour to be prayed, and this season needs no fixed day to be honoured. Some months the old heaviness still visits — a slowing, an ache, a pull inward — arriving on no schedule you can predict.

Ignatius asked only that we notice, not that we time it precisely. Where has God met you in this unscheduled descent? Begin your looking there, without needing to know when it will come again.
closing: Lord, sharpen my awareness even when the season keeps no calendar. Meet me in this unscheduled descent. Amen.

scripture.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

title: Letting the Review Wait
reflection:
Some months ask you to release what you're used to naming and reviewing on schedule — the count itself is gone, and with it, some of the certainty you used to examine your days by.

Ignatius's second movement is petition: asking God to illuminate what needs seeing, not what a calendar says should be seen. Let go of the tally today. Ask instead for light on whatever this unpredictable release is asking of you.
closing: Illuminate what this release asks of me, on its own timing rather than mine. I ask, without needing to count. Amen.

scripture.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

title: Consolation, Unscheduled
reflection:
Ignatian consolation was never defined by predictability — only by the movement toward God, whenever it arrives. A morning of returning energy, however irregular its timing, is still consolation. Still worth naming as such.

What feels, today, like a small return? Do not wait for it to prove itself reliable before you receive it as gift. Consolation does not need to repeat on schedule to be trusted.
closing: For this returning consolation, however it arrived, thank you. I receive it without demanding it explain its timing. Amen.

scripture.text: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.

title: Desolation Without a Countdown
reflection:
Ignatius taught that in desolation we make no major decisions — we wait, we stay faithful, we trust what we cannot yet see. That counsel holds even more when there is no known number of days left to wait through.

If today is heavy and formless, you are not failing an examination you no longer know how to take. You are being faithful in the not-yet. That is itself a kind of discernment.
closing: Even without a countdown, I choose to stay faithful in this waiting. You are present even when I cannot measure how long. Amen.

scripture.text: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
